pageCache.pageTitle: Chandler's Ford Infant School - Wrap Around Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Breakfast and After School clubs are offered every day by Rebecca's Out Of School Club.
Rebecca's is a fully inclusive out of school club for children aged between 4 and 12 attending Chandlers Ford Infant School and Merdon Junior School.
Operating since September 2005, they are based in the school on a Monday and Wednesday after school and at the 3rd Chandlers Ford Scout Hut and URC, Kings Road all other times. The club is run by a highly qualified and dedicated team who are committed to providing a high quality childcare facility where your children can have fun!
Rebecca's are Ofsted registered and you can see their inspection reports here
Breakfast sessions run from 7.30am until 9.00am. Afternoon sessions run from 3.15pm until 6.00pm.
Regular or one-off bookings are welcome.
For more information click here

pageCache.pageTitle: Chandler's Ford Infant School - Home Learning
pageCache.text:
Home Learning
At Chandler's Ford Infant School we believe that when learning is integrated between home and school, children grow and learn well. For this reason, we aim to ensure that any home learning set is clear, succinct and varied in order to suit all learning styles. Home learning should never be onerous but should support learning that has happened within class.
Home learning remains consistent throughout the child's time at Chandler's Ford Infant School and is as follows:
Please do come and talk to us if you have any questions or issues with any home learning that has been set. At Chandler's Ford Infant School we work together!
Remote Education Provision
During the recent pandemic, there was a period when school had to be closed. We are not anticipating a school closure. However, should that happen, no matter how short or extended, we will set specific home learning. This will be emailed to parents on the morning of the closure and will include varied activities linked to the children's learning in school.
This learning will also be accessible on the year group pages of the school website with clear instructions on how to communicate with the teacher during this time.
Please note that if your child is off school unwell, there is no expectation for them to complete home learning. Sometimes there needs to be a short period of recovery and rest before returning to school. However, if you think that your child is well enough then please discuss this with us.

PE and Sport Premium
PE and Sports Premium Spend
Sports Premium 2025-26
At Chandler's Ford Infant School our aim is for our children to develop healthy habits for life. We employ a sports coach to work alongside us so that children enjoy their PE and sports sessions. Our coach also works alongside teachers in order to develop their skills in teaching PE. We are committed to developing each child's physical, emotional and social well-being and we plan for this to happen, not only during PE sessions, but also during playtime and our outdoor lesson time. We believe that regular physical activity can develop a child's resilience and self-esteem and we aim to work with parents in order to promote and facilitate this.
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

pageCache.text:
Medical Needs
Our First Aid policy is updated on a yearly basis.
We have 1 member of staff who is has Emergency First Aid at Work training.
All of our lunchtime staff are first aid trained.
We have 6 paediatric first aid trained staff.
We have a first aid room where children can be given treatment whilst at school. If your child has a bump, especially to the head, we will communicate with you with an email at the end of the day via medical tracker. For more serious incidents we will communicate with you via telephone during the day.
If your child has a particular medical condition, please inform us straight away so we can administer the correct care.
If your child attends an after school club we will make sure to communicate with the leader of the club if necessary about an injury which has happened during the day.

Attendance
Coming to school every day helps children build strong friendships, develop good learning habits and make the most of what school has to offer. Even small amounts of time missed can add up and make it harder for children to keep up with their learning. We understand that sometimes absence is avoidable and we encourage parents to communicate with us when absence is necessary. We will positively work with families to support good attendance and ensure that each child has the best chance to succeed.
As a Chandler's Ford cluster of schools, we work closely together to encourage good attendance for all children. We have developed the following leaflet together which outlines attendance procedures, ensuring consistency for all children.
Chandler's Ford Schools attendance leaflet
Attendance Policy
Attendance Policy '25 in full
Attendance policy - summary for parents
Attendance Policy - Summary for Parents
Late Procedure
If you arrive after 8:55am for school the classroom doors will be locked, so bring your child to the school office to sign them in. If you arrive after 9.15am your child will be recorded as an unauthorised absence.
Absence Procedure
We understand that children will be unwell sometimes. If your child is not well enough to come to school, please phone the office before 9.30am on 023 80252655 or email us.
Requests for holiday leave in term time cannot be authorised, but requests for exceptional reasons may be authorised after careful consideration by the Head Teacher. For any period of pupil absence, we require a 'Request to authorise absence' form to be completed and returned to the school office as soon as you are able. This will be seen and actioned and returned to you once reviewed by the Head Teacher. The appropriate attendance mark will be entered on your child's attendance record. We keep you informed of your child’s attendance on a termly basis and work with families in times of difficulty to continue to promote good attendance

pageCache.pageTitle: Chandler's Ford Infant School - Our School Day
pageCache.text:
Our School Day
Doors open at 8.40am
Doors close at 8:50am
10.30-10.45am mid morning break
12.15-1.15pm lunch time
3.15pm end of school day
This equates to 32.5 hours spent in school.
The school office is open from 8.30am to 4pm.
The children can come into school from 8.40am. Year R and Year 1 children enter via their external classroom doors and Year 2 via the pupil door near the hall. The teachers greet the children and receive any messages from parents/carers at the door. Children are then greeted by teaching assistant in the classroom where they begin their morning jobs.
Any children arriving after 8:50am must be reported to the main office and are recorded as late. All external classroom doors are shut at 8:50am.
Children who arrive after 9.10am are recorded with an unauthorised absence.
Newsletters

SEND
Children With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
SEND Information Report
The SENDCo has prepared our school's SEND Information Report in collaboration with parents and Governors in accordance with Hampshire's Guidance for their "Local Offer". The legislation became statutory in August 2014.
All children's needs are catered for in our inclusive environment, be they physical, intellectual or emotional. We follow the National Code of Practice for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities and have a SENDCO and Learning Support Assistants to work with children and parents. Children who are currently working at a higher level of attainment are offered enrichment and extension activities, depending on their need.
SEND Provision
Our Inclusion Manager (SENDCo) Lisa Holmes, takes day to day responsibility for the provision made to individual children with SEND, working closely with staff, parents and carers, and other agencies.
In 2025, Ofsted reported 'Pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) are identified quickly. Where necessary, the school works closely with external agencies, such as educational psychologists and other specialists. Staff have strong relationships with pupils and their families. Staff help pupils with SEND to grow in confidence. They adapt provision in carefully considered ways.
sen@chandlersford-inf.hants.sch.uk
"The school provides a settled environment where pupils feel safe to learn and play."
In 2021, our Leading Learning Partner reported:
'The support for pupils with Special Educational Need (SEN) and other vulnerable pupils is well structured; informal contact with parents has been constructive in ensuring the emotional and learning needs are being addressed within the challenging context of the pandemic. Almost all of the more vulnerable pupils are in school. Inclusion leaders are well informed and proactive in ensuring disadvantaged pupils are well supported and challenged.'
Pupils with SEND are supported according to their individual needs and Learning Passports, (Individual Education Plans) are in place to monitor small steps of progress. Learning Passports are made with the child and with the teacher and parents agreeing on individual targets to work on. They are reviewed at least half termly and parents will receive a copy.
The school works closely with outside agencies to support pupils as required, such as Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists, Educational Psychologist, School Nurse.
Collaboration with parents is very valuable to us. Where pupils are included in a specific intervention parents are informed by letter from the Inclusion Manager, (SENDCO), personally by the class teacher or at parent consultations through the child’s Learning Passport. Parents can discuss their child’s progress with their class teacher, or alternatively arrange a meeting with the Inclusion Manager.
The school keeps a register of pupils with additional need which is updated half termly. This is called the SEND register.
Our Governing Body has important statutory duties towards pupils with SEND. The governing body assists in the development and monitoring of the school’s policies for Inclusion.

pageCache.text:
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development
Chandler’s Ford Infant School is a school which seeks to develop confident, independent, caring and enquiring individuals who are prepared for the future.
We believe in fostering life long learning through providing an environment that values mutual trust and respect, honesty and equality and seeks to develop everyone’s potential.
We will provide excellent learning opportunities for all and celebrate the successes of individuals and the whole community.
At Chandler’s Ford Infant School we believe spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (SMSC) underpins everything we do and through this we aim to prepare our children for life in modern Britain.
Our collective worship is delivered through daily assemblies:
Monday - whole school assembly
Tuesday - singing assembly
Wednesday - Class or yeargroup assembly
Thursday - Class or yeargroup assembly
Friday - Crown celebration assembly
Our Monday whole school assemblies are planned on a 3 year cycle so that each year builds on key themes such as: Awe Wonder and Reflection, Belonging, Behaviour and attitudes as well as celebrating key events and religions from around the world. It is a time when children are challenged to reflect and develop a respect for each other.
Wednesday and Thursday assemblies are linked to our Relationships and Health Education.
